final_answer:
I analyzed the provided GSE135251 hepatic RNA-seq cohort by building a 64,253-gene x 216-sample count matrix from the per-sample HTSeq files, parsing the GEO series-matrix metadata, and excluding the 10 healthy controls as instructed. This left 206 NAFLD cases for unsupervised analysis.

After filtering low-expression genes (CPM > 1 in at least 10% of cases), 14,823 genes remained. I normalized expression as log2-CPM and used the 5,000 most variable genes for PCA and hierarchical clustering (Ward linkage on the first 5 PCs). PCA explained 31.1% of variance on PC1 and 11.2% on PC2. Silhouette analysis supported a 2-cluster solution (silhouette 0.385), with cluster sizes 47 and 159.

The resulting transcriptomic clusters did not significantly differ by the requested disease-severity variables:
- Fibrosis stage: chi-square p = 0.3440
- NAS score: Kruskal-Wallis p = 0.8300
- NASH/NAFL group: chi-square p = 0.2069
- Early vs moderate disease grouping: chi-square p = 0.9959

Cluster compositions were broadly similar. Median NAS was 5.0 in both clusters, and median fibrosis stage was 2.0 in both clusters. A complementary PCA gradient check also did not show a significant association between PC1 and severity:
- PC1 vs fibrosis stage: Spearman rho = 0.0703, p = 0.3152
- PC1 vs NAS: Spearman rho = -0.0700, p = 0.3172

Conclusion: in this dataset, unsupervised clustering of normalized hepatic bulk transcriptomes produces a modest 2-cluster partition, but it does not meaningfully stratify NAFLD patients by fibrosis stage, NAS score, NASH stage, or early/moderate disease grouping. Thus, these unsupervised transcriptomic clusters do not provide strong evidence for clinically useful molecular subtypes aligned with disease severity in this cohort.
